sections.title: What this module covers
sections.body: Rails routing is the map between URLs and controller actions, and understanding it deeply is the difference between a developer who scaffolds routes and one who designs them. This page covers the seven RESTful routes that resources generates, nested routes and the two-level depth rule, member vs collection routes, namespace vs scope vs module, route constraints with regex and custom constraint objects, named routes and path/url helpers, and mounting Rack apps and engines. The routing interview question often comes in scenario form: 'your URL is 404 even though the route is in routes.rb — what do you check?' — and the answer requires understanding how Rails routes are matched top-to-bottom.

sections.title: Key topics and depth markers
sections.body: Topics: restful-routes, nested-routes, route-constraints, advanced-routing. Each topic has dedicated Q&A covering the concept, the comparison, the internal mechanics, and the scenario-based questions interviewers use to test production understanding.

sections.title: How interviewers probe this module
sections.body: Interviewers at Rails-focused companies probe these topics by opening with a definition question, then immediately following up with when would you use X vs Y? and what are the gotchas?. The depth marker is always the trade-off and the failure mode — not just the API surface.
